notes: "Vaxis Atom 500" is a two-piece wireless video kit (separate TX and RX units), not a single chassis, so ports are prefixed TX/RX above. This entry covers the base HDMI-only variant (VA20-500-TR01B, "Atom 500 HDMI Wireless Video Transmission Kit / Dual HDMI"): TX has 1x HDMI in + 1x HDMI loop-out; RX has 2x HDMI out. A separate "Atom 500 SDI" variant (VA20-S500-TR01B) exists with TX = 1x 3G-SDI in + 1x HDMI in, RX = 1x 3G-SDI out + 1x HDMI out — not included here since the request named "Atom 500" without the SDI qualifier; ask if the SDI variant is wanted instead. Both TX and RX are powered via USB-C (5V) and also accept a mounted Sony NP-F/L-series battery plate (no separate connector modeled for the battery plate, which is a mechanical mount, not a defined port type). No HDMI version (1.4/2.0/2.1) or USB power-delivery wattage is published by any source checked, so no "grade" was set on the HDMI or USB-C ports per instructions. Video support tops out at 1080p60 (H.265), consistent with HDMI 1.4-level bandwidth, but this is an inference, not a stated spec. Manufacturer's own product page (vaxis.us) lacked a structured spec table; B&H's spec pages returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, so port/format details were cross-verified across vaxis.us, Amazon listings, and Newsshooter's hands-on reviews (dimensions/weight/frequency/power figures came from the Newsshooter review coverage, not vaxis.us directly) — hence "medium" rather than "high" confidence. Antenna is described as built-in (non-removable, non-standard connector) so no antenna port was modeled.
